subject: Planned maintenance: us-east2 compatibility sweep and staggered node restarts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com>, Maya Lopez <sre@bigretail.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Planned maintenance: us-east2 compatibility sweep and staggered node restarts

Hi Jordan / Maya —

Quick heads-up: we have a planned maintenance operation in the us-east2 region next week to run a targeted kernel/driver compatibility sweep and apply a small driver patch that resolves an edge-case NVMe scheduling regression we've observed in a handful of hosts. This will be executed as a staggered, rolling restart across host pools to avoid capacity slips.

High-level details:
- Window: 2028-06-09 00:30 - 06:30 UTC (we will operate in staggered waves across availability zones)
- Expected user impact: minimal. We expect transient connection drops to affected instances during a node restart (seconds), with automatic traffic re-routing. No long-running requests should be interrupted if you pin model versions with graceful fallback enabled.
- Canary first: 3 nodes in zone-a for the first two hours, then expand if metrics are green.
- Mitigations: KV-cache preservation will be attempted where feasible; requests in flight will drain for up to 90s before eviction. We will hold a pre-window call if you have high-sensitivity traffic.

Attachments: us-east2-maintenance-runbook.pdf (runbook + rollback steps), kv-preservation-checklist.md, canary-schedule.csv

Ask from you: please reply if you have any production workloads you want moved out of the region during the window or if you'd like us to coordinate a pre-maintenance sanity call with your SREs. If we don’t hear back by EOD PT 2028-06-07 we’ll proceed with the standard canary plan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads-up. A couple quick questions from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether prefix/KV cache will be replayed or rehydrated automatically for pinned sessions? We have a handful of low-latency endpoints where a cold KV miss adds ~150ms and we'd like to avoid that for the canary.
2) Will there be any impact to replicated embeddings (we replicate across regions for redundancy)?

If it's useful, we can push a small subset of traffic to another region during the canary window; happy to hop on a 20-minute call today if that helps.

Jordan

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 12:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: us-east2 compatibility sweep and staggered node restarts

Jordan / Marissa —

Short answers:
- KV-cache: for the majority of model variants we will attempt an in-memory KV checkpoint and fast-rehydrate from an s3-backed snapshot for canary nodes. This reduces cold-miss penalty to ~30–50ms for rehydrated sessions. We cannot guarantee perfect preservation for all models (large multi-shard KV densities can still result in partial misses). See attached kv-preservation-checklist.md for the exact flow.
- Embeddings replication: embeddings stored in the managed vector layer are asynchronously replicated to the secondary region. Our maintenance does not touch long-term replication outside the host-level restarts; there should be no replication consistency window.

Operational notes for the canary wave (technical):
- Canary start: 2028-06-09 00:30 UTC — 3 nodes in zone-a (instance IDs: i-0a3f*, i-0b9c*, i-0c5d*)
- Health gates every 15 minutes: token latency, error-rate, KV hit-rate, and model load times. Automated rollback triggers on 3 consecutive threshold breaches.
- Drain behavior: requests will drain for up to 90s, then active sessions will be gracefully terminated if still present. We will tombstone cache entries and start rehydrate process immediately on the replacement host.

If Acme wants to shift a small percentage of traffic to us-east1 for the first canary hour that would give additional safety margin. Marissa — happy to take the prep call with Jordan and Maya later today (I’m free 14:30–16:00 PT).

—David
David Kim
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 9 Jun 2028 16:23:00 -0400
Subject: Final schedule confirmed — us-east2 maintenance (canary first hour)

Jordan / Maya —

Thanks for the quick responses and the call earlier. Final confirmation: the canary window will begin at 2028-06-09 00:30 UTC (3 nodes, zone-a) and expand in two-hour waves if all health gates pass. We've uploaded the final runbook and canary CSV to the Drive link in metadata and attached a short checklist.

What we did for Acme specifically:
- Marked your high-priority endpoints for KV rehydrate priority (you'll see faster rehydration as part of the canary).
- Coordinated with David to keep one warm fallback pool in us-east1 for your traffic during the first hour (no action required from you; we handled routing on our side).

If you notice any significant degradation during the canary please flag it immediately on this thread and we will pause expansion and initiate rollback.

Thanks again — we’ll post a short post-maintenance update to the status page once the sweep completes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
